type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

on_conflict.description: For an update: what happens when QuickBooks says the record changed after it was read (a stale edit sequence, 3200). ask (the default) pauses the run with a conflict prompt carrying the diff, which the app answers with overwrite (optionally with different params) or keep; overwrite re-sends with the current edit sequence without asking; fail raises error 3200 with the diff under response.error.conflict for the chart to handle. An update may leave edit_sequence out: the engine reads the record first and fills it in, and that read is the baseline the diff is judged against.

operation.description: A Semantic.Registry id, e.g. customer.query -- or a template that renders to one, such as \${input.find.operation}, checked when the state is entered.

paginate.description: Page through a query's results: the state raises `page` once per page (response.data that page's records, response.page its number from 1, response.more whether more follow), then `success` once every page is in (response.data the page set, response.count and response.pages its size). Only on a single `operation` that is a query (a create, update, delete or other operation has no results to page through, and one named by reference that renders to such fails the run before it is sent); `params` may not also set `iterator` or `max_returned`. A query QuickBooks does not iterate (the short lists such as account.query, the deleted-records queries, the company, preferences and host queries, the reports) is sent as it is and answers whole, which arrives as page 1 with `more` false, so a chart written for pages works over any query.

settle.description: Whether a request QuickBooks never answered is settled before the state raises anything: the engine finds out whether it was applied (a list add by its full name, a transaction add by the external_guid it stamps on it, an update by reading the record back, a delete by its id) and raises success as if the answer had arrived, re-sends, or raises error with type unsettled and the candidates when only the app can tell. false raises error with type no_response at once, as a query does when re-sending fails. Either way a no_response carries response.error.reason, why it went unanswered (timed_out or connector_error: it was sent, so QuickBooks may have applied it; rejected: QuickBooks could not read it; withdrawn: the app withdrew it before it was sent; page_expired: a later page never fetched), and, for an add, response.error.external_guid, the GUID it was sent with, so a chart that does its own looking can recognise the record. An add is stamped with a GUID whether settling is on or off.

as.description: The name the current element is bound to under each: each.line when as is line.

each.description: Run the child once per element of this list, one at a time and in order: a template that renders to a list, such as \${input.lines}. An empty list raises success at once with response.data []. At most 200 elements.

input.description: Rendered against this run's context and passed to the child as its input. With `each`, rendered once per element, with each.\<as>, each.index and each.count bound.

on_item_error.description: stop: the first child that fails raises error, with the outputs so far in response.data. continue: a failed element leaves null in response.data and an entry in response.errors, and the state still raises success.

stop_on.description: Endings of the called workflow, such as ["cancelled"], that end the loop: the first element whose run ends in one of them is the last, and the elements after it never start -- no requests, no questions. The state then raises success with the outputs up to and including that element in response.data, their endings in response.outcomes, and response.stopped: {index, outcome}, which element ended the loop and how (absent when every element ran). Not a failure, which on_item_error decides; each name must be an outcome the called workflow declares, or completed.

workflow.description: The key of another workflow of the same app to run as this step.

data.description: Any JSON, rendered as the state is entered and sent to the app as a workflow_run.notification webhook, to the webhook_url the run was started with (a run of a workflow that can send one is refused without it: 422 webhook_url_required). `response` here is the response of the event that entered the state -- on a paginated query's `page`, that page -- so `${response.data}` sends the page's records; a page set (a paginating query's `success`) cannot be sent. At most 4 MB once encoded. The run waits for the app's 2xx: then the state raises success with response.delivery_id (the same on every retry), response.seq (1, 2, ... in send order for the run) and response.attempts. Delivery is retried for about an hour (10 attempts); if none succeeds, or the data is over 4 MB, it raises error with response.error.type not_delivered or too_large.

kind.description: The list to look in: customer, vendor, employee, other_name, entity (those four together, one name space), item (every item type), account, class, or another reference list a transaction names (standard_terms, date_driven_terms, sales_tax_code, payment_method, ship_method, price_level, customer_type, vendor_type, job_type, sales_rep, customer_msg); or a template that renders to one, such as \${input.kind}.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

example.description: An example value, in the input's own JSON type: a string, a number, an object, or for a list the whole list. Nor does a list of objects a workflow state runs through (each: ${input.<name>}): its example is one element of what that workflow takes.

list.description: A list of what the rest of the declaration describes: with type operation, a list of that operation's bodies. The run input then takes an array, and each element is validated on its own.

operation.description: The operation this input is a body for. Left out, the input takes a pair -- {"operation": "customer.query", "params": {...}} -- validated against whichever operation the run names, which a request state sends with "operation": "\${input.\<name>.operation}" and "params": {"\$from": "\${input.\<name>.params}"}.

accounting_preferences.description: Accounting preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

closing_date.description: The company closing date set within the company file. (The QuickBooks Admin can assign a password restricting access to transactions that occurred before this date.)

is_assigning_journal_entry_numbers.description: If true, QuickBooks will automatically assign a number to each journal entry.

is_requiring_accounts.description: If `is_requiring_accounts` is true, a transaction can’t be recorded in the user interface unless it is assigned to an account. (However, transactions affected by this preference always require an account to be specified when added through the SDK.)

is_using_account_numbers.description: If true, an account number can be recorded for new accounts. If you include an account number in AccountAdd object when this preference is false, the account number will still be set, but won’t be visible in the user interface.

is_using_audit_trail.description: If true, QuickBooks will log all transaction changes in the audit trail report. If false, QuickBooks logs only the most recent version of each transaction.

is_using_class_tracking.description: If true, QuickBooks will include a “Class” field on all transactions.

current_app_access_rights.description: `current_app_access_rights` indicates whether auto-login has been allowed, the name of the auto-login user, and whether the application has been granted access to personal (sensitive) data.

automatic_login_user_name.description: If auto-login is allowed for this QuickBooks company file, `automatic_login_user_name` gives the user name that is allowed to use auto-login.

is_automatic_login_allowed.description: If `is_automatic_login_allowed` is true, then applications can use auto-login to access this QuickBooks company file.

is_personal_data_access_allowed.description: If true, then access is allowed to personal (sensitive) data in this QuickBooks company file.

finance_charge_preferences.description: Preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set for how finance charges are assessed against customers for late payment. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

annual_interest_rate.description: The interest rate, set by the QuickBooks user, that QuickBooks will use to calculate finance charges. The default value is 0.

calculate_charges_from.description: This preference is set by the QuickBooks user. Unless they change the value within QuickBooks, it will be DueDate.

finance_charge_account_ref.description: Refers to the name of the account used to track finance charges that customers pay. This is usually an income account. In a request, if a `finance_charge_account_ref` aggregate includes both `full_name` and `list_id`, `full_name` will be ignored.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

grace_period.description: The number of days before finance charges apply to customers’ overdue invoices. `grace_period` is set by the QuickBooks user, and has a default value (within QuickBooks) of 0.

is_assessing_for_overdue_charges.description: If true, finance charges are assessed on overdue finance charges. This preference is set by the QuickBooks user, and has a default value (within QuickBooks) of false. (Note that laws vary about whether a company can charge interest on overdue interest payments.)

is_marked_to_be_printed.description: If `is_marked_to_be_printed` is true, all newly created finance-charge invoices will be marked “To be printed.” (This makes it easier for the QuickBooks user to print a selection of invoices all at once.) This preference is set by the QuickBooks user, and has a default value within QuickBooks of false.

min_finance_charge.description: The minimum finance charge that will be applied regardless of the amount overdue. `min_finance_charge` is set by the QuickBooks user, and has a default value (within QuickBooks) of 0.

items_and_inventory_preferences.description: This aggregate contains the current item inventory settings for this company file.

enhanced_inventory_receiving_enabled.description: Indicator whether the enanched inventory receiving is turned on for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

fifo_effective_date.description: Date that FIFO (First In, First Out) is used to calculate the value of inventory sold and on-hand for this company file.

fifo_enabled.description: Indicator whether FIFO (First In, First Out) to calculate the value of inventory sold and on-hand is turned on for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_barcode_enabled.description: Indicator whether barcode are enabled for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_rsb_enabled.description: Indicator whether the bin tracking is turned on for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_on_build_assembly_enabled.description: Indicator whether the serial or lot number tracking is turned on for build assemblies in this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_on_inventory_adjustment_enab.description: Indicator whether the serial or lot number tracking is turned on for inventory adjustments in this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_on_purchase_transactions_ena.description: Indicator whether the serial or lot number tracking is turned on for purchase transactions in this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_on_sales_transactions_enable.description: Indicator whether the serial or lot number tracking is turned on for sales transactions in this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

jobs_and_estimates_preferences.description: Preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set about how to handle jobs and estimates. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

is_using_estimates.description: If true, this user is set up to create estimates for jobs.

is_using_progress_invoicing.description: If true, the QuickBooks user can create an invoice for only a portion of an estimate.

days_bills_are_due.description: By default, bills are due this many days after receipt.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

class_ref.description: Use classes to categorize transactions (for example, by department, location, or work type). Class tracking is off by default in QuickBooks. A `class_ref` points to one class; if both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored. In InvoiceAdd, a header-level `class_ref` is applied to line items unless you override or clear it on individual lines.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, `data_ext_name` will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because `owner_id` and `data_ext_name` together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same `owner_id` of zero, the `data_ext_name` must be a unique value among existing custom fields.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, `data_ext_type` must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of `data_ext_value` will depend on the `data_ext_type` of this data extension. For example, if `data_ext_type` is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of `data_ext_value` is 255 characters. If `data_ext_type` is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of `data_ext_value` is 1KB.

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

external_guid.description: Allows for the attachment of a user defined GUID value.

ship_method_ref.description: A shipping method, for example, standard mail or overnight delivery. A `ship_method_ref` aggregate refers to an item on the ShipMethod list. In a request, if a `ship_method_ref` aggregate includes both `full_name` and `list_id`, `full_name` will be ignored.

vendor_msg.description: Message to be printed on a purchase order for the vendor to read.

other2.description: Other, Other1, and Other2 are built-in transaction custom fields. Other is transaction-level; Other1 and Other2 are line-level. memo.description: This can be included in reports, but it doesn’t appear on the printed purchase order.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

WorkflowChart.description: A workflow is one JSON document: a Harel statechart whose states queue QuickBooks requests, pause for a decision from the calling app, or transform data. Qube.Workflows.Chart.validate/1 is the source of truth; this schema is documentation and a first-pass check.

input.description: What a run accepts. Validated at run start and published as a JSON Schema.

description.description: What this ending means, when its key does not say it already. Optional. Shown on the canvas, in the usage contract and in the guide.

kind.description: success: the run ends completed with this outcome. failure: the run ends failed with this outcome, and a workflow calling this one receives it as an error with response.outcome set.

output.description: Template rendered when the run ends this way, instead of the chart's own `output`. While it renders, `meta.outcome` holds the outcome key.

outcomes.description: Extra ways a run can end, beyond completed and failed. Each is a success (the default: the workflow worked as designed and this is how it ended; the run ends `completed` with this `outcome`) or, with `"kind": "failure"`, a named failure (the run ends `failed` with this `outcome`, and `error` is whatever the transition assigned to `error`, else the description, else `ended with outcome <key>`). A transition may target a declared outcome from anywhere, and no state at any level may use one of these keys.

output.description: Template evaluated against the final context when the run reaches `completed` or an outcome with no `output` of its own. Defaults to \${vars}. While it renders, `meta.outcome` holds the outcome key.

ui.description: Canvas bookkeeping for the chart itself, ignored by the engine: one entry per outcome placing its terminal node, and `transitions` placing the pills of the root's own handlers, keyed "\<event>|\<index>".

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-yes-with-a-warning).

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

createVendorCredit_response_json.description: QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer. A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-yes-with-a-warning).

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

ship_address_block.description: The address expressed as an address block of Addr1 through Addr5, depending on the number of lines in the original request that created the address.

addr1.description: The first line of an address.

addr2.description: The second line of an address (if a second line is needed).

addr3.description: The third line of an address (if a third line is needed).

addr4.description: The fourth line of an address (if a fourth line is needed).

addr5.description: The fifth line of an address (if a fifth line is needed).

time_modified.description: Time the object was last modified.

is_tax_included.description: For future use with international versions of QuickBooks.

customer_sales_tax_code_ref.description: Refers to the sales-tax code for sales related to this customer. (That is, it refers to a member of the SalesTaxCode list.) The sales-tax code indicates whether an item is taxable or non-taxable, and why. In a request, if a `customer_sales_tax_code_ref` aggregate includes both `full_name` and `list_id`, `full_name` will be ignored.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

is_to_be_printed.description: If `is_to_be_printed` is true, QuickBooks queues the form for later printing. It does not print immediately; printing is still a user action in QuickBooks.

is_fully_invoiced.description: If `is_fully_invoiced` is true, all the items in the sales order have been invoiced.

ref_number.description: `ref_number` is a user-managed transaction reference (for example, a check number). It can be edited and is not guaranteed to be globally unique. Some transaction types auto-populate `ref_number` when omitted, based on QuickBooks preferences and numbering state.

link_type.description: Indicates the nature of the link between the transactions:ltAMTTYPE means the two transactions are linked based on an amount value (for example an invoice linked to a payment).ltQUANTYPE means the two transactions are linked based on a quantity. This affects transactions that are linked to sales orders, estimates and purchase orders.

ref_number.description: `ref_number` is a user-managed transaction reference (for example, a check number). It can be edited and is not guaranteed to be globally unique. Some transaction types auto-populate `ref_number` when omitted, based on QuickBooks preferences and numbering state.

txn_date.description: The date of the transaction. In some cases, if you leave `txn_date` out of an -Add message, QuickBooks will prefill `txn_date` with the date of the last-saved transaction of the same type.

txn_id.description: `txn_id` is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. `txn_id` values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

txn_line_id.description: Identification number of the transaction line. (`txn_line_id` is supported as of v2.0 of the SDK. With qbXML v1.0 and v1.1, `txn_line_id` is always returned as zero.) If you need to add a new transaction line in a transaction Mod request, you can do so by setting the `txn_line_id` to -1.

txn_id.description: `txn_id` is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. `txn_id` values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

Represents a previously defined group of lines in the sales order. Compare with SalesOrderLine, which represents just one line in the sales order.

`sales_order_line_ret` and `sales_order_line_group_ret` combine: any number of each.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, `data_ext_name` will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because `owner_id` and `data_ext_name` together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same `owner_id` of zero, the `data_ext_name` must be a unique value among existing custom fields.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, `data_ext_type` must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of `data_ext_value` will depend on the `data_ext_type` of this data extension. For example, if `data_ext_type` is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of `data_ext_value` is 255 characters. If `data_ext_type` is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of `data_ext_value` is 1KB.

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

is_print_items_in_group.description: If true, a list of this group’s individual items their amounts will appear on printed forms.

item_group_ref.description: ItemGroup objects represent items that are grouped together for fast entry, and an `item_group_ref` aggregate refers to one of these item groups. In a request, if an `item_group_ref` aggregate includes both `full_name` and `list_id`, `full_name` will be ignored. You can use an ItemGroupQuery request to get information about all the item groups that are set up in the QuickBooks file.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, `data_ext_type` must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of `data_ext_value` will depend on the `data_ext_type` of this data extension. For example, if `data_ext_type` is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of `data_ext_value` is 255 characters. If `data_ext_type` is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of `data_ext_value` is 1KB.

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-yes-with-a-warning).

message.description: QuickBooks' own statusMessage, such as which field it did not support.

code.description: QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

message.description: QuickBooks' own statusMessage.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

updateSalesReceipt_response_json.description: QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer. Only an `Error` severity from QuickBooks is `status: "error"` (and makes the request's `state` `error`), so a query that matched nothing is still `success`. A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

You can provide a structured address (Addr1-Addr3 plus City/State/`postal_code`/etc.) or use block mode (Addr1-Addr5 only). Do not mix block mode with other address fields. In block mode, each Addr line prints as its own line and is returned in `ship_address_block` or `bill_address_block`.

country.description: The country name in an address, or, in returned Host information (HostRet or HostInfo), the country for which this edition of QuickBooks was designed. (Possible values are US, CA, UK, and AU.)

note.description: In a `bill_address` or `ship_address` aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

state.description: The state name in an address.

fob.description: QuickBooks uses the term FOB, “freight on board,” to indicate the place from which the product is shipped. The FOB has no accounting implications.

credit_card_txn_info.description: Contains data from the credit card transaction used in the payment. This data originates from a previous qbmsXML credit card transaction. The data following the element `credit_card_txn_input_info`” data is the data from the original qbmsXML request. The “`credit_card_txn_result_info`” is the data from the original qbmsXML response.

credit_card_txn_input_info.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. This value is returned in the QBMS response to a QBMS transaction request, and must be subsequently supplied by your application in the QB SDK ReceivePaymentAdd or SalesReceiptAdd request.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. You should save this value without modification and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you want to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

txn_authorization_time.description: Timestamp indicating the time in which the card processor authorized the transaction.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, `data_ext_name` will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because `owner_id` and `data_ext_name` together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same `owner_id` of zero, the `data_ext_name` must be a unique value among existing custom fields.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, `data_ext_type` must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of `data_ext_value` will depend on the `data_ext_type` of this data extension. For example, if `data_ext_type` is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of `data_ext_value` is 255 characters. If `data_ext_type` is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of `data_ext_value` is 1KB.

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

rate.description:

It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. This value is returned in the QBMS response to a QBMS transaction request, and must be subsequently supplied by your application in the QB SDK ReceivePaymentAdd or SalesReceiptAdd request.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. You should save this value without modification and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you want to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

txn_authorization_time.description: Timestamp indicating the time in which the card processor authorized the transaction.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, `data_ext_name` will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because `owner_id` and `data_ext_name` together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same `owner_id` of zero, the `data_ext_name` must be a unique value among existing custom fields.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, `data_ext_type` must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of `data_ext_value` will depend on the `data_ext_type` of this data extension. For example, if `data_ext_type` is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of `data_ext_value` is 255 characters. If `data_ext_type` is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of `data_ext_value` is 1KB.

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

credit_card_txn_input_info.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

template_ref.description: QuickBooks templates specify how to print certain transactions. A template query returns the names of all templates that have been defined in QuickBooks. A `template_ref` element refers to one of these templates.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

exchange_rate.description: `exchange_rate` is the rate from this currency to the company’s home currency at AsOfDate. You can supply a rate when adding transactions, but QuickBooks does not provide rates through the SDK. If your home currency is USD and internet access is available, rates can be downloaded in the QuickBooks UI via Lists > Currency > Activities > Download Latest Exchange Rates.

total_amount.description: Subtotal plus `sales_tax_total`.

ship_date.description: The date when the product was, or will be, shipped.

payment_method_ref.description: `payment_method_ref` identifies how a payment is made (for example, cash, check, or card type). If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored.

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

txn_id.description: `txn_id` is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. `txn_id` values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

external_guid.description: Allows for the attachment of a user defined GUID value.

txn_number.description: An identifying number for this transaction.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

listGeneralSummaryReports_response_json.description: QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer. Only an `Error` severity from QuickBooks is `status: "error"` (and makes the request's `state` `error`), so a query that matched nothing is still `success`. A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

col_id.description: An identifying number that corresponds to the position of this column in the report. The columns are numbered from left to right, starting with 1.

col_type.description: The type of data that this column contains. `col_type` values are formatted types. (Returned ctPercent values, for example, will have digits after the decimal points, and ctAddr1 values will be strings.)

data_type.description: The data type: IDTYPE, STRTYPE, and so on.

num_col_title_rows.description: The number of rows to allocate for column titles. Although this number is usually 1, with some reports it is 2 or 3. (For an example of column titles that span multiple rows, look at a ProfitAndLossByJob report in QuickBooks.)

num_columns.description: The number of columns in the report.

num_rows.description: The number of rows in the report.

report_basis.description: If `report_basis` is rbCash, the report bases income and expenses on the dates when money changed hands.rbAccrual, the report bases income on the dates when customers were invoiced and bases expenses on the dates when bills were entered.rbNone, the report uses the default `report_basis`, which is either the QuickBooks Preference setting or the QuickBooks default for a given type of report.

report_data.description: If the report contains any data, it is given row-by-row in a `report_data` aggregate.

data_row.description:
A data row contains the actual data for each column.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_data.description: `row_data` describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

subtotal_row.description:
A row that contains a calculated subtotal of the data in all the rows since the last SubTotalRow and, usually, a single underline. There can be multiple SubTotalRow aggregates in a report.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_data.description: `row_data` describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

text_row.description:
A text row contains only text and is used mainly for headings.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

total_row.description:
A row that contains a calculated total of all the data that has come before and a double underline. There will only be one `total_row` per report. If `total_row` doesn’t include any numerical values, the columns required to show the total values aren’t part of the report. These columns weren’t included when the report was customized.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

report_title.description: The main title for this report.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, `data_ext_name` will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, `data_ext_type` must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of `data_ext_value` will depend on the `data_ext_type` of this data extension. For example, if `data_ext_type` is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of `data_ext_value` is 255 characters. If `data_ext_type` is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of `data_ext_value` is 1KB.

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-yes-with-a-warning).

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).
