credit_card_txn_info.description: Contains data from the credit card transaction used in the payment. This data originates from a previous qbmsXML credit card transaction. The data following the element `credit_card_txn_input_info`” data is the data from the original qbmsXML request. The “`credit_card_txn_result_info`” is the data from the original qbmsXML response.

credit_card_txn_input_info.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. This value is returned in the QBMS response to a QBMS transaction request, and must be subsequently supplied by your application in the QB SDK ReceivePaymentAdd or SalesReceiptAdd request.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. You should save this value without modification and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you want to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

txn_authorization_time.description: Timestamp indicating the time in which the card processor authorized the transaction.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

cancel_reason.description: Why the run was cancelled, when a reason was given.

current_state.description: Where the run is: the leaf state path, and while a workflow it calls is running, on into that workflow -- `<calling state> / <state in the called workflow>`, such as `create_customer / resolve_conflict.find_holder`. Null once it has ended.

links.description: `self` (this run), `decisions` (answer a question), `cancel` (stop the run) and `ui` (the run in QuBeSync).

decisions.description: Where to answer. While the run is `awaiting_input`, it carries the current prompt's `token` as `?prompt_token=`, so an answer POSTed to it can only answer that question: once the run has asked again it is refused with `409 prompt_changed`.

outcome.description: How the run ended, once it has. With state completed: completed, or a success the workflow declares (such as cancelled) -- it worked as designed and this is how it ended. With state failed: failed, or a failure the workflow declares (such as customer_over_limit) -- something needs attention, and this names what. Null while the run is still going.

prompt.description: Present while awaiting_input: `id` (the question's id, as the workflow's contract lists it -- its path from this run, `<calling state> / <wait state>`, when a workflow this one calls asked), `token` (new each time the run asks; send it back as the decision's `prompt_token`), `kind`, message, data and the options to choose from. `from` is set when a workflow this one calls asked the question: `workflow` (its key) and `state` (its own wait state) -- that workflow runs as part of this run, so answer it here either way. When the asking workflow runs once per item of a list, `from` also carries `item_index` (0-based) and `item_count`. `kind` says who asked: `decision` for a `wait` state's own question, `conflict` when the engine asks about an update that met a stale edit sequence (someone changed the record in QuickBooks after the run read it, error 3200) and the state's `on_conflict` is `ask`, its default. A conflict prompt's `id` is `conflict:<state>` (prefixed like any question when a workflow this one calls asked), `state` is the request state that sent the update, and `data` carries `operation` (the update, e.g. `customer.update`), `sent` (the fields it carries, without its id and edit sequence), `current` (the record QuickBooks has now, with its edit sequence), `as_read` (the record as the run last read it, or null when it never read it), `conflicts` (one `{field, sent, current, as_read}` row per field being updated that someone else changed too) and `theirs` (one `{field, as_read, current}` row per field they changed that the update does not touch; empty when `as_read` is null). Its options are fixed: `overwrite` re-sends with the current edit sequence -- the original fields, or `data.params` (an object, optional) in their place -- and `keep` carries on with the record as QuickBooks has it.

kind.description: decision: a wait state's own question. conflict: the engine asks about an update that met a stale edit sequence; see the prompt's description.

token.description: This asking of the question: new every time the run asks, the same question asked again included (a `wait` in a loop, a workflow called once per item, another conflict). Send it as the decision's `prompt_token`, and an answer that arrives after the run has asked again is refused instead of taken for the new question. Opaque: compare it only for equality.

state.description: running means it is working -- a QuickBooks request is in flight, or a workflow it calls is running as part of it; awaiting_input means it needs a decision from you, whichever part of it asked. cancelled means somebody stopped it (`POST .../cancel`); `outcome` stays null and `cancel_reason` says why, when they said.

summary.description: Set once the run has ended (completed, failed or cancelled): what it did. Null while it is going.

workflow.description: The key of the workflow this is a run of. Still set when that workflow has been deleted: the run is kept, readable by its id until retention removes it.

listInventoryAdjustments_response_json.description: QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer. Only an `Error` severity from QuickBooks is `status: "error"` (and makes the request's `state` `error`), so a query that matched nothing is still `success`. A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

backing_off.description: `true` while the Web Connector's last tries couldn't open QuickBooks (on that computer it's closed, or a dialog is open) and QuBe Sync is spacing its tries out, up to 30 minutes apart. `next_check_in_expected_at` is the next try. It ends at the first session that reaches QuickBooks, and clicking Update Selected in the Web Connector tries straight away.

onboarding.description: Send the user here to connect QuickBooks. `null` once used, or if never generated.

ui.description: This connection in the QuBe Sync dashboard.

next_check_in_expected_at.description: When the Web Connector is next expected to check in and pick up queued requests, worked out from its last check-in, its schedule and any wait QuBe Sync gave it: every 10 seconds for `realtime`, every 5 minutes for `standard`, up to 30 minutes apart while `backing_off`, and slower while a sandbox app's `realtime` connection has nothing to do (`next_check_in_reason`). A request queued now is picked up then. `null` before the first check-in, and for a `simulated` connection that isn't backing off, since it runs as soon as a request is queued. A time more than a minute past means the check-in is late: a long session is still running (one of your requests is `sent`), or the Web Connector isn't running on the QuickBooks computer.

next_check_in_reason.description: What set `next_check_in_expected_at`. `schedule`: the connection's own pace. `backing_off`: the Web Connector's last tries couldn't open QuickBooks, as `backing_off`. `sandbox_idle`: a `realtime` connection in a sandbox app slows down while it has nothing to do, to once a minute after 10 minutes without a request and every 5 minutes after an hour; the request you queue is picked up at that next check-in, and from then it's back to every 10 seconds. Clicking Update Selected in the Web Connector runs it at once. `null` when `next_check_in_expected_at` is.

redirect_url.description: Where onboarding sends the user when they finish, cancel, or open an expired link. QuBe Sync appends `?connection_id=<id>&state=connected` (or `state=cancelled`, `state=expired`) to it as it is.

type.description: How QuickBooks is reached: `standard` (Web Connector polls every 5 minutes), `realtime` (every 10 seconds), or `simulated` (a fake QuickBooks answered by QuBe Sync itself -- connected immediately, no Web Connector -- see the CLI/Quickstart guides; in beta: it doesn't match real QuickBooks in every case yet).

username.description: Generated automatically; this is what the Web Connector authenticates as.

listJobReports_response_json.description: QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer. Only an `Error` severity from QuickBooks is `status: "error"` (and makes the request's `state` `error`), so a query that matched nothing is still `success`. A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

col_id.description: An identifying number that corresponds to the position of this column in the report. The columns are numbered from left to right, starting with 1.

col_type.description: The type of data that this column contains. `col_type` values are formatted types. (Returned ctPercent values, for example, will have digits after the decimal points, and ctAddr1 values will be strings.)

data_type.description: The data type: IDTYPE, STRTYPE, and so on.

num_col_title_rows.description: The number of rows to allocate for column titles. Although this number is usually 1, with some reports it is 2 or 3. (For an example of column titles that span multiple rows, look at a ProfitAndLossByJob report in QuickBooks.)

num_columns.description: The number of columns in the report.

num_rows.description: The number of rows in the report.

report_basis.description: If `report_basis` is rbCash, the report bases income and expenses on the dates when money changed hands.rbAccrual, the report bases income on the dates when customers were invoiced and bases expenses on the dates when bills were entered.rbNone, the report uses the default `report_basis`, which is either the QuickBooks Preference setting or the QuickBooks default for a given type of report.

report_data.description: If the report contains any data, it is given row-by-row in a `report_data` aggregate.

data_row.description:
A data row contains the actual data for each column.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_data.description: `row_data` describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

subtotal_row.description:
A row that contains a calculated subtotal of the data in all the rows since the last SubTotalRow and, usually, a single underline. There can be multiple SubTotalRow aggregates in a report.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_data.description: `row_data` describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

text_row.description:
A text row contains only text and is used mainly for headings.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

total_row.description:
A row that contains a calculated total of all the data that has come before and a double underline. There will only be one `total_row` per report. If `total_row` doesn’t include any numerical values, the columns required to show the total values aren’t part of the report. These columns weren’t included when the report was customized.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

report_title.description: The main title for this report.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.

* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

WorkflowRunEvent.description: One thing that happened in a run you started, or in a workflow it calls -- which runs as part of it, so its events are in the same stream, right after the `call_started` event that began it. Append-only.

item_index.description: Only inside an element of a state that runs a workflow once per item: which element (0-based).

kind.description: `call_started` and `call_finished` begin and end a workflow this one calls; `run_started` and `run_completed`/`run_failed`/`run_cancelled` with a `state` are that workflow's own start and end, at the calling state. `notification_queued`, `notification_delivered` and `notification_failed` are a notify state's `workflow_run.notification`: sent, answered with a 2xx, or never delivered. `match_waiting` and `match_answered` are a match state's: waiting for the connection's name index to be built or refreshed, and what it found (its tier and counts, never a name).

payload.description: What the kind carries: `response` (the whole response) on response_received -- except a paginated query's last one, which has `count` and `pages` in place of `data`, the records being on each page_delivered, `owner`/`event`/`index`/`description`/`target`/`to`/`considered` on transition_taken, `assigned` on assigns_applied, `option`/`data`/`by` on decision_received, `page`/`count`/`queued_request_id`/`response` on page_delivered (a paginated query's page, raised as `page`; `response` is that page's, as on response_received), `workflow` (and `item_index`/`item_count`) on call_started and call_finished, with `stops: true` on the call_finished of the element whose ending (one of the state's `stop_on`) ended the loop, `delivery_id`/`name`/`seq`/`bytes` on notification_queued, notification_delivered (with `attempts`) and notification_failed (with `attempts` and `error`, whose `type` is `not_delivered` or `too_large`; one too large was never sent and has no `seq`) -- never what was sent, `for` (`build` or `refresh`) on match_waiting, `match` (the tier), `candidates`, `candidates_total`, `candidates_total_complete` and `index` (`ready`, or `unavailable` when it asked QuickBooks' own filters) on match_answered -- never a name, and so on. A `response` that succeeded but that QuickBooks warned about has `warning` with its `code` and `message` (530, for one: a field it does not support, which it saved the record without). A `response` that is an error has `error` with `code`, `type` and `message`; when `type` is `no_response` (QuickBooks never answered) it also has `reason`, why: `timed_out` or `connector_error` (sent, so QuickBooks may have applied it), `rejected` (QuickBooks could not read it), `withdrawn` (withdrawn before it was sent) or `page_expired` (a later page never fetched), and, for an add, `external_guid`, the GUID it was sent with. Response bodies are removed 7 days after the run ends.

seq.description: Its position in the stream, which is the order entries come in and what `after` takes: `7` is the run's own 7th event, `7.2` the 2nd event of the workflow the 7th started, `7.3.1` a level deeper.

state.description: Where it happened, as a path from the run you started: `create_customer / try_create` is a state of the workflow `create_customer` calls. Null for what happened to the run as a whole.

vars_after.description: `vars` of the workflow it belongs to once this event had happened. Null 7 days after the run ends.

workflow.description: The key of the workflow whose chart the event belongs to.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

WorkflowRunSummary.description: What a finished run did -- a workflow it calls runs as part of it, so what that workflow did is in these lists too, where the call sits in the run's order, under its path (`<calling state> / <state>`). Cancelling never undoes anything in QuickBooks: `side_effects` is what the run had already changed, and `unconfirmed` what it may have.

calls.description: Every workflow the run called, the ones those called included, in order: the calling state's path, the element when that state runs once per item, the workflow it called and how that ended. What each did is in the lists above.

item_index.description: Which element of the list the call ran for, when the calling state runs once per item; null otherwise.

outcome.description: How the called workflow ended: completed, failed, or an outcome it declares. Null when it was cancelled.

state.description: The calling state, as a path from this run.

workflow.description: The key of the workflow it called.

decisions.description: Every answer the run was given, in order.

item_index.description: Only inside an element of a state that runs a workflow once per item: which element (0-based).

state.description: Where it happened, as a path from this run: a state of this workflow, or `<calling state> / <state>` inside a workflow it calls.

workflow.description: The key of the workflow whose state that is.

discarded.description: Requests that were queued but not yet sent when the run was cancelled, and were withdrawn; and, for a state that runs a workflow once per item, how many items never started.

item_index.description: Only inside an element of a state that runs a workflow once per item: which element (0-based).

items_not_started.description: For a state running once per item: the elements after the cancelled one.

message.description: For items not started, e.g. "2 items of ensure_items not started".

state.description: Where it happened, as a path from this run: a state of this workflow, or `<calling state> / <state>` inside a workflow it calls.

workflow.description: The key of the workflow whose state that is.

matches.description: Only when the run's match states answered, the workflows it called included, in order: what each one found -- its tier and counts, never a name.

candidates.description: How many candidates the answer listed (at most 10).

index.description: `ready`: answered from the connection's name index. `unavailable`: the connection has none (it isn't realtime), so QuickBooks' own filters answered.

item_index.description: Inside a state that runs a workflow once per item: which element (0-based).

state.description: The match state's path from the run you started.

workflow.description: The key of the workflow whose state it is.

notifications.description: Only when the run's notify states sent the app anything, the workflows it called included: how many `workflow_run.notification` webhooks were delivered (`sent`) and how many never were (`failed`: every attempt failed, or the data was over 4 MB).

requests.description: Every QuickBooks request the run sent, in order. `status` is `success`, `error`, or `in_flight` for one already sent when the run was cancelled (it may still complete). A paginated query is one entry, with `pages`. A request whose answer was lost and that was then found applied reads as `success`, with `settled` and the record found: whether the run's own check found it, or a later query of the chart's own answered with the record the add carried (its `external_guid`, or for a list add sent without one, its full name), which `found_by` names. A change whose answer was lost and that nothing settled keeps `error` and has `unconfirmed`.

evidence.description: With `settled`, when the run settled it itself: on what grounds, in a sentence -- what the check looked at, what came back and what that means, such as `of 2 candidates with reference number "1044", one carries the GUID sent (txn_id 2-1), so the add was applied`. The same sentence is `response.evidence` in the chart and on the run's `settled` event.
evidence.example: of 2 candidates with reference number "1044", one carries the GUID sent (txn_id 2-1), so the add was applied

found_by.description: Only on an add whose answer was lost and that the chart's own lookup found afterwards (`settle: false`): the state whose answer carried the record the add was sent with. The add reads as `success`, with that record's identifiers, and is a side effect.

identifiers.description: Whichever of `list_id`, `txn_id`, `full_name` and `ref_number` QuickBooks returned for the record.

item_index.description: Only inside an element of a state that runs a workflow once per item: which element (0-based).

pages.description: Only for a paginated query: how many pages it took. `status` is how the last one went.

role.description: Only for a request the run sent on its own to settle a lost answer or a conflict: `settle` a check, `resend` the request again, `reapply` or `overwrite` an update sent again with the current edit sequence, `prepare` the read before an update. Absent for the state's own request.

settled.description: Only on a state's own request whose answer was lost, or that met a conflict: how the run settled it, as `response.settled` says. `found` is also what an add reads when a later query of the chart's own found it (`found_by`).

state.description: Where it happened, as a path from this run: a state of this workflow, or `<calling state> / <state>` inside a workflow it calls.

unconfirmed.description: Only `true`, on a create, update, delete or execute QuickBooks never answered (its computer lost its connection, or QuickBooks or the Web Connector was closed, while it had the request; nothing reports an error) that the run neither found applied nor sent again. It may or may not have changed QuickBooks; it is listed under `unconfirmed`, not `side_effects`.

workflow.description: The key of the workflow whose state that is.

side_effects.description: The successful creates, updates, deletes and executes, wherever in the run they happened: the `requests` entries with `status` `success`. One whose answer was lost and that was found applied afterwards is here too, with `settled`.

evidence.description: With `settled`, when the run settled it itself: on what grounds, in a sentence, as the request's `evidence` says.

identifiers.description: Whichever of `list_id`, `txn_id`, `full_name` and `ref_number` QuickBooks returned for the record.

item_index.description: Only inside an element of a state that runs a workflow once per item: which element (0-based).

settled.description: Only when QuickBooks' answer was lost and the change was found applied afterwards, by the run's own check or the chart's own lookup: how, as the request's `settled` says.

state.description: Where it happened, as a path from this run: a state of this workflow, or `<calling state> / <state>` inside a workflow it calls.

workflow.description: The key of the workflow whose state that is.

stopped_at.description: The state the run was in when it ended -- a path into the workflow it called when it ended while one was running.

unconfirmed.description: Only when there is one: the creates, updates, deletes and executes QuickBooks never answered that the run neither found applied nor sent again -- the chart asked your app and it picked another record, say, or the run failed or was cancelled first. Each may or may not have changed QuickBooks, so it is not in `side_effects`: check QuickBooks before sending it again. The `requests` entry is the same, with `unconfirmed`.

state.description: Where it was sent, as a path from this run: a state of this workflow, or `<calling state> / <state>` inside a workflow it calls.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-yes-with-a-warning).

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

WorkflowChartTemplate.description: Any JSON value. Strings may hold \${...} references; a map may hold the reserved "\$from" key, whose rendered map the rest of the map is deep-merged onto. A map holding "\$map" is a list built from another: {"\$map": "\${vars.items}", "as": "item", "template": ...} renders template once per element, with the element at each.\<as>, its position at each.index and the length at each.count. {"\$add": [a, b, ...]} is the sum of its operands and {"\$default": [a, b, ...]} the first candidate that renders to something. {"\$merge": [a, b, ...]} deep-merges each object onto the ones before it, as "\$from" does (objects merge key by key; lists and scalars replace; an operand that renders to nothing is skipped). {"\$find": "\${vars.items}", "as": "item", "where": condition} is the first element the condition holds for, with the element at each.\<as>, or nothing. {"\$refs": "\${input.params}", "operation": "invoice.create"} lists an add's references, or with "list_ids" puts their ListIDs back. No other \$-prefixed key is allowed.

$add.description: The sum of its operands: numbers, or templates that render to numbers; nothing counts as 0.

$default.description: The first of its candidates that renders to something other than nothing or an empty string.

$find.description: A template that renders to a list. With "where" (a condition, required) and "as" (default item): the first element for which the condition holds, the element at each.\<as>, each.index and each.count; nothing when none does. Only \$find, as and where.

$merge.description: Objects, or templates that render to objects, each deep-merged onto the ones before it: objects merge key by key, lists and scalars replace. An operand that renders to nothing is skipped. Alone in its object.

$refs.description: An add's params (an object, or a template for one). With "operation" (the add's operation id, or a template; required): the distinct references the params make, in the order they first appear -- every *_ref field the operation has, its kind derived from the field's name (customer_ref is customer, ar_account_ref account, item_group_ref item_group), one entry per kind and full name with every path it appears at: {kind, field, full_name, name, parent, list_id, paths}. A kind with no full-name lookup (template) is left out. With "adds" (a list of {kind, add}, as ensure takes them) and "rules" (an object of kind to ensure, create or must_exist; ensure by default), each also has "rule", "ensure": {kind, add}, the add from adds that makes it, one of its name alone under create, or none, and "pick", true when there is no add. With "list_ids" instead (one per reference, in that order), it is the params, every reference replaced by {"list_id": ...}. "unresolved": true keeps only the references sent without a ListID, in either. Only \$refs, operation, adds, rules, list_ids and unresolved.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

NameIndex.description: QuBe Sync's index of the names in this connection's company file, for finding records by name (see Match a name): customers, vendors, employees and other names, items, accounts, classes, and the other lists a transaction names (terms, sales tax codes, payment and ship methods, price levels, customer, vendor and job types, sales reps and customer messages). Only `realtime` and `simulated` connections can have one, and it is built the first time something on the connection needs matching: a match, or opting in (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/name-index`). QuBe Sync then reads the lists from QuickBooks itself, a step at a time, and your requests always go first; those reads never appear among your requests and never send a webhook. An index unused for 30 days is deleted, and built again the next time it's needed.

as_of.description: When the index last caught up with QuickBooks: changes made in QuickBooks since then aren't in it yet. While it's used, it catches up after a Web Connector session that brought your requests, at most every 5 minutes. `null` unless `ready`.

records.description: How many records the index holds; while `building`, how many are in so far. `null` when `not_built` or `unavailable`.

state.description: `ready`: every list is in. `building`: QuBe Sync is reading the lists from QuickBooks, the first time, or again after the connection was pointed at another company file, went 90 days without your requests, or a build gave up. `not_built`: nothing on the connection has needed matching yet, or the index went unused for 30 days and was deleted. `unavailable`: the connection is `standard`, which can't have one.

QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

The workflows a template calls report their own. Null for a workflow whose chart has never been a version of a shipped template, such as one you wrote, or adapted from a template before saving it.

key.description: The template's key, as `GET /workflow-templates/{key}` takes it.

status.description: About the working copy, which is what installing again replaces; `working_copy_changed` says whether the published version has caught up. `up_to_date`: the template has not changed since, or this is its current chart. `update_available`: the template has changed and this chart has not, so installing it again loses nothing. `update_available_customized`: the template has changed, and so has this chart since it was installed; installing again discards those edits, so compare it with the template first. `removed`: QuBe Sync no longer ships that template; the workflow keeps working as it is.

working_copy_changed.description: True when the working copy would run differently from the published version. Canvas positions do not count.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US
