WorkflowRunWebhookPayload.description: The body QuBeSync POSTs to a run's `webhook_url`, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` like every other QuBeSync webhook. One flat envelope for every event, always about the run the app started -- a workflow it calls runs as part of it and sends none of its own. `GET links.run` returns the whole run. `workflow_run.notification` is data a notify state sends the app mid-run: the run waits for a 2xx before it goes on, so notifications arrive one at a time, in `seq` order, all before the run's ending webhook; a failed delivery is retried for about an hour (10 attempts) with the same `delivery_id`.

data.description: Only on `workflow_run.notification`: the notify state's `data`, rendered -- any JSON, at most 4 MB.

delivery_id.description: Only on `workflow_run.notification`: the notification's id, the same on every retry of it. Deduplicate on it: delivery is at least once.

error.description: Only on `workflow_run.completed`, `workflow_run.failed` and `workflow_run.cancelled`.

from.description: Only on `workflow_run.notification`: null when the run's own workflow sent it; when a workflow it calls did, which -- `workflow`, its own `state`, and `item_index`/`item_count` inside a state that runs once per item -- as `prompt.from` says. Never a run id: `run_id` is always the run the app started.

links.description: `run` returns the whole run; `decisions` is where to answer; `cancel` stops the run; `ui` opens it in QuBeSync.

decisions.description: Where to answer. While the run is `awaiting_input`, it carries the current prompt's `token` as `?prompt_token=`, so an answer POSTed to it can only answer that question: once the run has asked again it is refused with `409 prompt_changed`.

name.description: Only on `workflow_run.notification`: the notify state's `name`, what the app routes on, such as `customers_page`.

outcome.description: Only on the endings; null on `workflow_run.cancelled`.

prompt.description: Only on `workflow_run.awaiting_input`: the question, exactly as `prompt` on the run -- `id`, `token`, `kind`, `message`, `data`, `options`, and `from` (`workflow`, `state`) when a workflow this one calls asked. `kind` is `decision` for a wait state's own question and `conflict` when the engine asks about an update whose record someone changed after the run read it (a stale edit sequence, 3200): then `state` names the request state, `data` carries `operation`, `sent`, `current`, `as_read` (null when the run never read the record), `conflicts` and `theirs`, and the options are always `overwrite` (optionally with `data.params`, the fields to send instead) and `keep`. See `prompt` on WorkflowRun.

kind.description: decision: a wait state's own question. conflict: the engine asks about an update that met a stale edit sequence; see the prompt's description.

token.description: This asking of the question, as `prompt.token` on the run: send it as the decision's `prompt_token`.

seq.description: Only on `workflow_run.notification`: 1, 2, 3... for the run, in the order its notifications were sent, the workflows it calls included.

state.description: Only on `workflow_run.notification`: the notify state's path from the run, on into a workflow it calls (`sync_page / send_customer`), as a question's `id` is.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; also the `t=` in the signature header.

workflow.description: The workflow's key -- still set after that workflow has been deleted.

workflow_id.description: The workflow's id. Null once that workflow has been deleted -- its runs are kept, run to the end on the version they started with, and still name it in `workflow` -- and for a built-in chart, which has no workflow row.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

ship_address.description: This aggregate supports at most five address lines. You can provide a structured address (Addr1-Addr3 plus City/State/`postal_code`/etc.) or use block mode (Addr1-Addr5 only). Do not mix block mode with other address fields. In block mode, each Addr line prints as its own line and is returned in `ship_address_block` or `bill_address_block`.

addr1.description: The first line of an address.

addr2.description: The second line of an address (if a second line is needed).

addr3.description: The third line of an address (if a third line is needed).

addr4.description: The fourth line of an address (if a fourth line is needed).

addr5.description: The fifth line of an address (if a fifth line is needed).

city.description: The city name in an address.

country.description: The country name in an address, or, in returned Host information (HostRet or HostInfo), the country for which this edition of QuickBooks was designed. (Possible values are US, CA, UK, and AU.)

note.description: In a `bill_address` or `ship_address` aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

postal_code.description: The postal code in an address.

state.description: The state name in an address.

fob.description: QuickBooks uses the term FOB, “freight on board,” to indicate the place from which the product is shipped. The FOB has no accounting implications.

bill_address.description: This aggregate supports at most five address lines. You can provide a structured address (Addr1-Addr3 plus City/State/`postal_code`/etc.) or use block mode (Addr1-Addr5 only). Do not mix block mode with other address fields. In block mode, each Addr line prints as its own line and is returned in `ship_address_block` or `bill_address_block`.

addr1.description: The first line of an address.

addr2.description: The second line of an address (if a second line is needed).

addr3.description: The third line of an address (if a third line is needed).

addr4.description: The fourth line of an address (if a fourth line is needed).

addr5.description: The fifth line of an address (if a fifth line is needed).

city.description: The city name in an address.

country.description: The country name in an address, or, in returned Host information (HostRet or HostInfo), the country for which this edition of QuickBooks was designed. (Possible values are US, CA, UK, and AU.)

note.description: In a `bill_address` or `ship_address` aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

postal_code.description: The postal code in an address.

state.description: The state name in an address.

invoice_line_ret.description:
Represents one line in the invoice. Compare with InvoiceLineGroup, which represents a previously defined group of lines in the invoice.

`invoice_line_ret` and `invoice_line_group_ret` combine: any number of each.

class_ref.description: Use classes to categorize transactions (for example, by department, location, or work type). Class tracking is off by default in QuickBooks. A `class_ref` points to one class; if both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored. In InvoiceAdd, a header-level `class_ref` is applied to line items unless you override or clear it on individual lines.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, `data_ext_name` will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because `owner_id` and `data_ext_name` together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same `owner_id` of zero, the `data_ext_name` must be a unique value among existing custom fields.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, `data_ext_type` must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of `data_ext_value` will depend on the `data_ext_type` of this data extension. For example, if `data_ext_type` is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of `data_ext_value` is 255 characters. If `data_ext_type` is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of `data_ext_value` is 1KB.

owner_id.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

rate.description:

message.description:

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-yes-with-a-warning).

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-yes-with-a-warning).

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

listAgingReports_response_json.description: QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer. Only an `Error` severity from QuickBooks is `status: "error"` (and makes the request's `state` `error`), so a query that matched nothing is still `success`. A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

col_id.description: An identifying number that corresponds to the position of this column in the report. The columns are numbered from left to right, starting with 1.

col_type.description: The type of data that this column contains. `col_type` values are formatted types. (Returned ctPercent values, for example, will have digits after the decimal points, and ctAddr1 values will be strings.)

data_type.description: The data type: IDTYPE, STRTYPE, and so on.

num_col_title_rows.description: The number of rows to allocate for column titles. Although this number is usually 1, with some reports it is 2 or 3. (For an example of column titles that span multiple rows, look at a ProfitAndLossByJob report in QuickBooks.)

num_columns.description: The number of columns in the report.

num_rows.description: The number of rows in the report.

report_basis.description: If `report_basis` is rbCash, the report bases income and expenses on the dates when money changed hands. rbAccrual, the report bases income on the dates when customers were invoiced and bases expenses on the dates when bills were entered. rbNone, the report uses the default `report_basis`, which is either the QuickBooks Preference setting or the QuickBooks default for a given type of report.

report_data.description: If the report contains any data, it is given row-by-row in a `report_data` aggregate.

data_row.description:
A data row contains the actual data for each column.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_data.description: `row_data` describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

subtotal_row.description:
A row that contains a calculated subtotal of the data in all the rows since the last SubTotalRow and, usually, a single underline. There can be multiple SubTotalRow aggregates in a report.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_data.description: `row_data` describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

text_row.description:
A text row contains only text and is used mainly for headings.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

total_row.description:
A row that contains a calculated total of all the data that has come before and a double underline. There will only be one `total_row` per report. If `total_row` doesn’t include any numerical values, the columns required to show the total values aren’t part of the report. These columns weren’t included when the report was customized.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

report_title.description: The main title for this report.

* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.

What each means and how to handle it: [Error handling](https://docs.qubesync.com/error_handling#quickbooks-said-no).

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field.
* `invalid_amount` (3040): QuickBooks couldn't read an amount: it was written without its two decimals, such as 40 for 40.00, which the qbXML schema allows and QuickBooks doesn't. The message names the value and the field.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...).
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records.

info.description:
A single generic operation surface for every curated qbXML request QuBe Sync supports, driven directly off the qbXML schema -- see the [MCP server](/mcp-server) to explore available operations interactively.

**Every endpoint queues a request and returns it immediately (`201`, a `QueuedRequest`).** QuickBooks Desktop is reached through the customer's Web Connector, which polls QuBe Sync, so the answer arrives seconds to minutes later. **Pass a `webhook_url` with every request**: when QuickBooks has answered, QuBe Sync POSTs the same document to it -- `state` set, `response_json` filled in -- signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (see the Webhooks guide). `response_json` is the `{status, data}` envelope documented on each operation: `status: "success"` with `data` derived from the qbXML `*Ret` (and `warning`, QuickBooks' code and message, when it carried the request out but warned about it), or `status: "error"` with QuickBooks' own status code and message -- a QuickBooks business error is a *successful* HTTP round trip. `links.self` returns the request on demand (for a dashboard, a retry, a script); it is not the integration path. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header with each request so a call whose answer you never got can be sent again without queueing it twice.

Authentication is HTTP Basic with your app's API key as the username and a blank password. Connections themselves (creating one, onboarding, its QWC file and password) are the `/connections` endpoints; every QuickBooks operation is scoped to one of them.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. post.description:
Usually, you'll want to use the pre-built operation endpoints, but if you really need qbXML we have you covered.

Rules for raw qbXML
1. It has no DOCTYPE: qbXML doesn't use one.
2. It declares its qbXML version, such as `<?qbxml version="16.0"?>`, and the version is 13.0, 14.0, 15.0 or 16.0.
3. It is valid against that version's qbXML schema.
4. `<QBXML>` holds only `<QBXMLMsgsRq>`, with at least one request inside it.
5. In a batch (two or more requests), no request has an `iterator` attribute: queue an iterator query on its own.
6. `onError` is `stopOnError` or `continueOnError`. QuickBooks Desktop refuses `rollbackOnError` for the whole envelope.

A single request request answers exactly as an operation does: `response_json` is the same `{status, data}` summary, and a request QuickBooks refuses ends `error`. An iterator query (`iterator="Start"` with `MaxReturned`), alone in its envelope, is paged as usual, one webhook per page.

A batch's (multiple requests inside one QBXMLMsgsRq envelope) `response_json` is `{status, responses}`: one entry per request, in the order they were sent, with `request` (the request's name), `request_id` (its `requestID`, or `null`) and `status`. An answered entry is `success` or `error`, with the `data`, `message`, `warning` or `error` one request's summary has. `not_processed` is a request QuickBooks skipped: with `onError="stopOnError"` QuickBooks stops at the first request that fails and answers every request after it "The request has not been processed." (status 3231), so each of those is `not_processed`, while `continueOnError` carries on and runs each one. A 3231 that isn't after an earlier failure is QuickBooks declining that request itself (its edition or preferences don't allow it), so it's an `error`. The top-level `status` is `success` only when every entry is.

A batch QuickBooks answered is `response_received`, whatever its entries say: some of its requests may have been carried out. Read the entries to see which, and don't resend the whole batch.

Send one with every request: it is how answers are delivered. Optional only so a script can queue and look up `links.self` by hand. It must be an absolute http or https URL. It may not contain a username or password, and in production it may not point at localhost or a private, loopback or link-local address.

An `Idempotency-Key` that isn't 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters, or that was already used for a different request, is refused in a sentence naming the header.

post.description:
Finds the records in the connection's company file a name could mean, ranked, from QuBe Sync's index of the file's names (the connection's `name_index`). QuickBooks itself only looks a name up exactly, or by "contains" on one list at a time. A match also ignores case, accents, punctuation, company suffixes such as Inc and LLC, spacing and word order, ranks near matches, and can compare an account number, email, phone, city and postal code. It's answered at once, from the index as it stands: `index.as_of` says how current that is.

`match` is the first tier that applies: `exact`, `strong`, `candidates` or `none` (see the response). Use an `exact` match as it is, and confirm anything else with a person, or with what your app knows. A strong match is likely, not certain: `Acme Inc` and `Acme LLC` are strong for each other. Inactive records are matched too, with `is_active: false`.

Numbers in names count: `Subway #1235` is never offered for `Subway #1234`, and `Subway Store 1234` finds `Subway #1234`. In a file of near-identical names, such as numbered locations, `candidates_total` says how many records qualified: when that's more than a person can choose from, ask for what tells them apart (the number, a city, a postal code, an account number) and match again with it. `exact_only` answers only `exact` or `none`, and `min_score` moves the candidate threshold for one call.

Match a record once. When it's confirmed, keep its `list_id` on your own record and refer to it by that from then on (`customer_ref: {list_id}`): a `list_id` survives renames. Match again only when a stored `list_id` stops working, because the record was deleted or merged.

Only `realtime` and `simulated` connections can match (422 `matching_requires_realtime`). The first match on a connection starts building its index, and until it's in every match is refused with 409 `name_index_building`. To have it ready ahead of time, and be told when it is, opt in with `POST /connections/{connection_id}/name-index` and a `webhook_url`. Every match counts as a use: an index is kept current while it was used in the last 7 days, and deleted after 30 days unused.

Send the names in the JSON body: a match in the query string is refused, since URLs end up in logs. QuBe Sync doesn't log them either. A match changes nothing, so it takes no `Idempotency-Key`.

parameters.name: connection_id

a_store.summary: A numbered location, with its city

any_name.summary: Any customer, vendor, employee or other name

by_account_number.summary: By your own id, kept in the account number

exact_only.description: `true` answers only `exact` or `none`: the one record with this full name, as QuickBooks compares names, or nothing. Never a fuzzy match, so its answer can be used without asking. `fields` are ignored.

fields.description: For customers, vendors, employees and other names (`customer`, `vendor`, `employee`, `other_name` and `entity`): what else your app knows about the record. The same `account_number` makes a strong match whatever the name. The same `email`, `phone` or `postal_code`, with a name at least 0.4 alike, makes a strong match. Each one in common is a reason and ranks a candidate higher; `company_name` and `city` do only that. An email's or account number's case doesn't count, nor a phone's punctuation, country code or extension, nor a postal code's spaces or a US ZIP+4's last four digits. The `city` and `postal_code` are compared with the record's billing address (a vendor's, employee's or other name's own address).

account_number.description: The record's account number in QuickBooks. An app that creates the records can set it to its own id, and match on it later, if the company doesn't use the field for something else.

company_name.description: Compared once punctuation and suffixes are set aside. Not for `employee`: QuickBooks employees have no company name.

kind.description: Which lists to look in. `entity` is customers, vendors, employees and other names together, which share one name space in QuickBooks; `item` is every item type. Any other kind is its own list.

min_score.description: This call's candidate threshold, in place of 0.44: raise it to list only close names, lower it (down to 0.3, the least alike a match reads) to list more. A record that's a candidate for another reason (two letters swapped, or strong but not alone) stays one, and `exact` and `strong` don't change. Not taken with `exact_only: true`.

name.description: The name your app has for the record: its own name, without its parent's when you send `parent`. Without a `parent`, a full name such as `Smith:Kitchen` is matched exactly too. Its words with a digit (a store, unit or job number, such as `1234` in `Subway #1234`) must agree with a record's, leading zeros aside.

parent.description: For a job, a sub-item, a subaccount or the like: its parent's full name or ListID, so only that parent's children are matched. Without one, children match on their own name too, with a reason naming the parent. Taken for `customer`, `entity`, `item`, `account`, `class`, `customer_type`, `vendor_type` and `job_type`. A parent the index doesn't hold matches nothing.

post.description:
Has QuBe Sync build the connection's name index now, so it's ready before your first match, and tells you when it is. QuBe Sync reads the names in the connection's lists from QuickBooks itself, a step at a time, as the Web Connector checks in, and your own requests always go first. That takes a few Web Connector sessions, more on a large company file.

While it builds the answer is `202`. Pass a `webhook_url` to be sent `name_index.ready` once it's in, or `name_index.failed` if the build gives up (see the callback). Calling this again while it builds replaces the `webhook_url`, and starts nothing more. On an index that's already `ready` the answer is `200`, and nothing is sent. So it's safe to repeat, and takes no `Idempotency-Key`.

Only `realtime` and `simulated` connections can have an index (422 `matching_requires_realtime`). An index is kept current while it was used in the last 7 days, and deleted after 30 days unused: a match counts as a use, and so does this.

post.description:
`option` is one of the ids the run's `prompt.options` listed; `data` carries whatever that option declared `fields` for. A question asked by a workflow this one calls (`prompt.from`) is part of this run, and is answered here the same way. A conflict prompt (`prompt.kind` is `conflict`: an update met a record someone changed after the run read it) is answered here too, with one of its two fixed options: `{"option": "overwrite"}` re-sends the update with the current edit sequence and the fields it sent, `{"option": "overwrite", "data": {"params": {...}}}` sends those fields instead (a merge worked out from `prompt.data`: an object of fields the update takes, like `prompt.data.sent`; one it does not take is refused with a 422, `invalid_data`, naming the field, and the run keeps waiting), and `{"option": "keep"}` leaves QuickBooks as it is and carries on with its record.

POST to the run's `links.decisions`: while the run is asking, it carries the prompt's `token` as `?prompt_token=`, so an answer you send again because the first got no response can't be taken for the run's next question. `token` is new every time the run asks, the same question asked again included (a `wait` in a loop, a workflow called once per item), and an answer naming a question the run is no longer asking is refused with `409 prompt_changed`, changing nothing. Building the URL yourself, send the token as `prompt_token` in the query or the body (the body's wins); without one, an answer is taken for whatever the run is asking when it arrives.

When the run has asked again since -- the same question from a loop, or the next item's -- the answer is refused with `409 prompt_changed` and nothing changes. Leave it out (or null), with no `prompt_token` in the query either, to answer whatever the run is asking when it arrives.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. get.description:
qbXML: `AccountQueryRq`.

Finds accounts in the chart of accounts, all of them or those of one `account_type`, each with its parent account. It returns an account's own details, not its transactions. When the company shows account numbers, a `full_name` made of digits can match the account with that number rather than that name.

If you are querying for an account whose `full_name` contains a number, the query might return an account that has a matching account number rather than a matching `full_name`. For example, if you are querying for an account named 12345, and 12345 happens to be the account number of a totally different account, the query won’t return what you asked for (the account named 12345), but instead will return the account with the account number 12345.

This problem won’t happen if:

- the “show account numbers” preference is turned off in the QuickBooks file, or
- the account name exactly matches the account number. (In this case, query would return the correct account either way.)

To avoid this problem:

- Don’t name an account using a number unless the number exactly matches the account’s account number.
- If an account name must contain a number that doesn’t match its own account number, have the QuickBooks user change the account’s name slightly, for example to 12345a.

Intuit's reference: [AccountQuery](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/accountquery).

post.description:
qbXML: `AccountAddRq`. The `account_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

This message allows you to perform the same activities as a user does in the QB New Account form, which can be accessed in QB by selecting Lists->Chart of Accounts->Accounts->New. If you want the account to be a subaccount to an existing account, similar to using the SubAccount checkbox and selection list drop down in the New Account form, you use the `parent_ref` aggregate. Notice that the `parent_ref` can take either the parent account’s `list_id` or `full_name`.

It is important to note that the parent account specified in the `parent_ref` must have the same account type (`account_type`) of the child account that you are creating. (The `account_type` field maps to the Type pulldown menu in the New Accounts field.) The `account_number` is NOT the account number assigned by your bank or other entity. (That number is specified in the `bank_number` field.) The account number is simply part of a numbering scheme used by accounting systems to help provide a visual hierarchy and ordering of all of the accounts in a Chart of Accounts. QuickBooks provides this functionality for those who need or want it, but by default has this functionality turned off. The `account_number` field maps to the Number field in the New Account form, which appears only if the Accounting preferences for the company have been set to use account numbering. By default, account numbers aren’t used. In the SDK, you can set the account numbers if you want, even if the preference for it has been turned off. The numbers would then appear later if the user turned this preference on. In the `open_balance` field for certain types of new Accounts, you may want to leave the opening balance at 0 if you are going to fund the account from another account. That process will effectively create the opening balance. How do you increase and decrease amounts in bank accounts?

Intuit's reference, linked below, has the rest of these notes.

Intuit's reference: [AccountAdd](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/accountadd).

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

addr3.description: The third line of an address (if a third line is needed).

addr4.description: The fourth line of an address (if a fourth line is needed).

addr5.description: The fifth line of an address (if a fifth line is needed).

city.description: The city name in an address.

country.description: The country name in an address, or, in returned Host information (HostRet or HostInfo), the country for which this edition of QuickBooks was designed. (Possible values are US, CA, UK, and AU.)

note.description: In a BillAddress or ShipAddress aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

postal_code.description: The postal code in an address.

state.description: The state name in an address.

ar_account_ref.description: `ar_account_ref` points to an Accounts Receivable account. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

credit_card_txn_info.description: Contains data from the credit card transaction used in the payment. This data originates from a previous qbmsXML credit card transaction. The data following the element `credit_card_txn_input_info`” data is the data from the original qbmsXML request. The “`credit_card_txn_result_info`” is the data from the original qbmsXML response.

credit_card_txn_input_info.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. This value is returned in the QBMS response to a QBMS transaction request, and must be subsequently supplied by your application in the QB SDK ReceivePaymentAdd or SalesReceiptAdd request.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. You should save this value without modification and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you want to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

txn_authorization_time.description: Timestamp indicating the time in which the card processor authorized the transaction.

customer_ref.description: `customer_ref` identifies a customer or customer job. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored. In SalesReceipt and ReceivePayment, it identifies who receives credit. In TimeTracking, it identifies who the time can be billed to and is required in TimeTrackingAdd when IsBillable is true.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

def_macro.description: `def_macro` lets you assign a reusable name to a returned `txn_id` or TxnLineID so later requests can reference it with `useMacro`. This feature requires SDK 2.0+.

exchange_rate.description: `exchange_rate` is the rate from this currency to the company’s home currency at AsOfDate. You can supply a rate when adding transactions, but QuickBooks does not provide rates through the SDK. If your home currency is USD and internet access is available, rates can be downloaded in the QuickBooks UI via Lists > Currency > Activities > Download Latest Exchange Rates.

external_guid.description: Allows for the attachment of a user defined GUID value.

payment_method_ref.description: `payment_method_ref` identifies how a payment is made (for example, cash, check, or card type). If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

ref_number.description: `ref_number` is a user-managed transaction reference (for example, a check number). It can be edited and is not guaranteed to be globally unique. Some transaction types auto-populate `ref_number` when omitted, based on QuickBooks preferences and numbering state.

refund_amount.description: Specifies the amount to be taken from the credit transaction you are linking via this aggregate. The amount specified in this aggregate can’t exceed the amount of the credit transaction you are linking. If you supply an amount that exceeds, you’ll get a runtime error.

txn_id.description: `txn_id` is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. `txn_id` values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

refund_from_account_ref.description: In an ARRefundCreditCardAdd, the account which is the source of funds for the credit card refund. Normally this is Undeposited Funds. However, you can specify another account if you wish. If you specify nothing here, Undeposited Funds is used by default.

QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

request_id.description: Your own label for the request, sent to QuickBooks as its qbXML `requestID` and echoed in the raw answer (`response_xml`); optional, since the answer's webhook already carries the request's `id`.

txn_date.description: The date of the transaction. In some cases, if you leave `txn_date` out of an -Add message, QuickBooks will prefill `txn_date` with the date of the last-saved transaction of the same type.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

get.description:
qbXML: `BillPaymentCheckQueryRq`, from qbXML 2.0.

Provides functionality found in the Find/Advanced Find window to find bill payments paid by check. The Find/Advanced Find windows can be reached by clicking the Find button on the main QuickBooks menubar, by selecting Edit->Find, or simply by using the shortcut CTRL-F. Notice that you can use the `meta_data` attribute inside the query tag if you want only a count of the bill payments that will be returned from the query.

If you know the bill payment transaction ID or reference number, you could use these, or search by transaction date, or search by the date where the bill was last modified.

If you need additional filters, you can use the entity filter to search for bills from a specific vendor or vendor sub (using the `list_id_with_children` or `full_name_with_children` tags). You can also search for bills entered against a particular account (the `ap_account_ref` specified in the originating BillAdd request). You can specify all subaccounts by using the various \*WithChildren tags. For example, to find all bills entered against Checking where you have multiple checking accounts, you would use the `list_id_with_children` or `full_name_with_children` tags inside your `account_filter` tags. Finally, you can filter on the `ref_number` or `ref_number` range. Notice that all of these filters can be used together (ANDed) if desired.

To prevent the return of too much data, you can use `max_returned` to limit the total number of bills returned from the query. In addition, you can limit the type of data that is returned for each bill, using `include_ret_element`. Finally, you can specify whether each bill contains line items using the `include_line_items`, which by default is False (no line item data).

Intuit's reference: [BillPaymentCheckQuery](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/billpaymentcheckquery).

But if numbers have been used as account names, confusion could arise.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`.
