When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

Choose at most one of: `list_id`, or `full_name`, or the set (`active_status`, `class_filter`, `from_modified_date`, `max_returned`, `name_filter`, `name_range_filter`, `to_modified_date`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: max_returned

parameters.description:
Filters according to the object’s Name.

Choose at most one of: `list_id`, or `full_name`, or the set (`active_status`, `class_filter`, `from_modified_date`, `max_returned`, `name_filter`, `name_range_filter`, `to_modified_date`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: name_filter

name.description: The string to match.

parameters.description:

parameters.name: to_modified_date

parameters.description: `owner_id` identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same `owner_id` and `data_ext_name`, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.
parameters.name: owner_id

parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`. Send one with every request: it is how answers are delivered. Optional only so a script can queue and look up `links.self` by hand. It must be an absolute http or https URL. It may not contain a username or password, and in production it may not point at localhost or a private, loopback or link-local address.
parameters.name: webhook_url

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

qbXML: `ItemSalesTaxAddRq`. The `item_sales_tax_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Adds a sales-tax item, which is an item used to calculate a single sales tax that is collected at a specified rate and paid to a single agency. (Compare with the ItemSalesTaxGroupAdd message.) An ItemSalesTaxRef aggregate refers to an item on this list. In a request, if an ItemSalesTaxRef aggregate includes both `full_name` and `list_id`, `full_name` will be ignored.

See also: [Line item taxes](https://docs.qubesync.com/quickbooks-notes#line-item-taxes).

Intuit's reference: [ItemSalesTaxAdd](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/itemsalestaxadd).

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).

* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. About `sales_or_purchase_mod` versus `sales_and_purchase_mod` in an ItemServiceMod request:

You can’t change the reimbursable status of a service item through the SDK. For example, if a service item is marked as non-reimbursable in QuickBooks, you can’t send a modify request that includes a `sales_and_purchase_mod` aggregate. Similarly, if you send an ItemServiceAdd request that includes a `sales_or_purchase` aggregate, you can’t later modify that item using a `sales_and_purchase_mod` aggregate.

Starting with qbXML spec 7.0, you can modify the various account references using the appropriate account reference aggregate and the matching Apply Account RefToExistingTxns boolean. You need to use the boolean when you change an account ref because the QuickBooks UI displays a prompt asking whether the change should apply to existing transactions or not. Specifying True for the boolean basically dismisses this with a “Yes” answer, allowing your changes to be made and changes any existing transactions that use the item with that `account_ref`. Specifying “False” means that the mod won’t take affect if there are existing transactions.

Setting this to “True” should be used with caution and normally only after some user has indicated that they want those changes made to all those existing transactions!

If any affected transactions are protected by a closing date and password, the `account_ref` changes won’t be made and so the Mod request will return an error without making the requested Mod.

QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. qbXML: `ItemQueryRq`.

Finds items of every type in one query: service, inventory, non-inventory, other charge, discount, group and the rest. Filter by `list_id`, `full_name` or name. For an inventory item's current quantity on hand, query inventory items instead: this query doesn't reflect what other transactions did to it.

Notice that you can’t get an inventory asset value from QuickBooks using this query. Instead, you need to use the General Summary Report query (which currently doesn’t include Assembly Items).

Suppose you needed a way to search for the amount on hand of items that have had their amount changed since a certain date. Again, you wouldn’t use this query, but a GeneralDetailReportQuery that has its GeneralDetailReportType set to “InventoryValuationDetail.” This will tell you which items changed by how much.

Finally, suppose you wanted the on-hand quantity from QB as of a specific date. You would use a General Summary Report of the type Inventory Valuation Summary. (Again, this report doesn’t include Inventory Assemblies.)

get.description:
qbXML: `JournalEntryQueryRq`.

In traditional accounting, transactions are entered into the general journal and categorized exclusively by account. In QuickBooks, most transactions can be categorized either by account or by type (invoice, check, and so on). For a few activities in QuickBooks, you must use the general journal directly, for example for recording depreciation.

Notice that you must supply the credit line and a corresponding debit line in the same request. It won’t work to supply them in two distinct requests. You can supply as many credit lines and debit lines in one single request as you want so long as the total monetary amount from the credits equals the total monetary amount from the debits in that request.

Finally, DO NOT supply negative sign for the monetary amounts. QuickBooks does that for you. If you do supply the negative sign amounts will add instead of cancel and you’ll get a runtime error.

### Querying for Condensed Transactions

If you need the query to return condensed transactions, you can do this by using either an Entity or Account filter in the journal query request. Alternatively, you could use the The generic TransactionQuery, which can return condensed transactions.

Intuit's reference: [JournalEntryQuery](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/journalentryquery).

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

post.description:
qbXML: `JournalEntryAddRq`. The `journal_entry_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

In versions 1.0 and 1.1, all debit lines in a JournalEntryAdd request had to appear first, followed by all credit lines. But in versions 2.0 and above, the debit and credit lines can be intermingled. A credit line can legally come first in thejournal entry add.

In traditional accounting, transactions are entered into the general journal and categorized exclusively by account. In QuickBooks, most transactions can be categorized either by account or by type (invoice, check, and so on). For a few activities in QuickBooks, you must use the general journal directly, for example for recording depreciation.

Notice that you must supply the credit line and a corresponding debit line in the same request. It won’t work to supply them in two distinct requests. You can supply as many credit lines and debit lines in one single request as you want so long as the total monetary amount from the credits equals the total monetary amount from the debits in that request.

Finally, DO NOT supply negative sign for the monetary amounts. QuickBooks does that for you. If you do supply the negative sign amounts will add instead of cancel and you’ll get a runtime error.

### Querying for Condensed Transactions

If you need the query to return condensed transactions, you can do this by using either an Entity or Account filter in the journal query request. Alternatively, you could use the The generic TransactionQuery, which can return condensed transactions.

If the transaction is a home currency adjustment, QuickBooks will ignore the `is_amounts_entered_in_home_currency`, `currency_ref`, and `exchange_rate` elements.

Intuit's reference: [JournalEntryAdd](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/journalentryadd).

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

get.description:
qbXML: `ListDeletedQueryRq`, from qbXML 2.0.

A ListDeletedQuery will return all list elements deleted within the last 90 days, grouped according to object type.

If you are synchronizing deletes, you might want to specify `list_del_type` elements in order of dependency in a ListDeletedQuery request; for example, first specify a `list_del_type` of Item, then specify a `list_del_type` of Vendor. This way the SDK will return Item deletes before Vendor deletes (both in order of real delete times). Item depends on (refers to) to Vendor, so by having the Item deletes returned first you avoid a dependency problem.

By default, the records of each type are returned in ascending order, according to the “real” delete time. For example:

- If list object A is deleted at 10 a.m. and list object B is deleted at 11 a.m., the query request will return A first, then B.
- However, if the QuickBooks user moves the clock back before deleting B (for example, B is deleted at 9 a.m.), the query will still return first A then B, because B was deleted after A in “real” time.

Intuit's reference: [ListDeletedQuery](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/listdeletedquery).

qbXML: `ListMergeRq`, from qbXML 7.0.

This request merges one list object into another list object of the same type. Currently you can merge customers/jobs, or vendors, or accounts. The consequence of the merge is that only the merge-to object remains. The merge-from object goes away and all transactions that reference that merge-from object now reference only the merge-to object.

The request itself is very simple: you just need the `list_id` and `edit_sequence` for the two objects to be merged. However, you may have to do some preliminary work on the objects themselves before the merge. For accounts, you must make sure they have the same AccountType, and must stop if they don’t. (You can’t change the AccountType!) You must also check the Sublevel of the two accounts and change one of them to match the other before, by making the ParentRef point to the same parent account or by getting rid of the ParentRef, if you need to set the Sublevel to 0.

For customers, you must make sure only one of the customers/jobs has child jobs. If both have child jobs, you must move the jobs first to the merge-to customer or delete the jobs.

You can only merge two list objects from a QuickBooks company file if the file is open in single-user mode. If the file is open in multiuser mode, your application will receive an error.

Intuit's reference: [ListMerge](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/listmerge).

parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`. parameters.name: webhook_url

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

qbXML: `PaymentMethodAddRq`. The `payment_method_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Adds a payment method, which is the way a customer pays for goods or services, for example, cash, check, or Master Card. A PaymentMethodRef aggregate refers to an item on the PaymentMethod list. In a request, if a PaymentMethodRef aggregate includes both FullName and `list_id`, FullName will be ignored.

In a SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, or ARRefundCreditCard request that contains credit card transaction data supplied from QBMS transaction responses, you must specify the payment method, and the payment method must be a credit card type.

Intuit's reference: [PaymentMethodAdd](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/paymentmethodadd).

post.description:
qbXML: `ReceivePaymentAddRq`, from qbXML 1.1. The `receive_payment_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Records a customer's payment. Set `customer_ref`, `total_amount` and either `is_auto_apply` (to an invoice of that exact amount, else the oldest) or `applied_to_txn_add`: each invoice's `txn_id` and the amount paid, at most what it owes (more fails with 3210 `invalid_value`) and at most `total_amount` in all. A line can also apply a credit memo (`set_credit`); a `total_amount` of 0 that only does that creates no payment and answers just each invoice's txn_id and txn_type. A payment gets no number unless you send `ref_number`. Without `deposit_to_account_ref` it goes to Undeposited Funds.

1. To record a customer’s payment against an invoice for one or more jobs,
2. To set a discount (for early payment, for example),
3. To set a credit (from previously returned merchandise, for example).

If full payment is received at the time of sale, it is recorded using a sales receipt transaction, not a receive payments transaction.

Notice that access to sensitive data permissions aren’t required to use this request. However, if the application doesn’t have access to sensitive data permission, then the response returned won’t contain certain sensitive data. For example, even if credit card data is supplied in the ReceivePaymentAdd request via the `credit_card_txn_info` aggregate, the response won’t contain the corresponding aggregate.

This request can be used to record QBMS credit card transaction data, via the `credit_card_txn_info` aggregate. You can record charges and also authorizations. (You can later respond to a QBMS capture of authorized charges by doing a ReceivePaymentMod and changing the `credit_card_txn_type` to “Charge”.)

Intuit's reference, linked below, has the rest of these notes.

Intuit's reference: [ReceivePaymentAdd](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/receivepaymentadd).

is_auto_apply.description: If `is_auto_apply` is true, QuickBooks applies `total_amount` to any outstanding transaction that exactly matches `total_amount`. If no exact match is found, the payment is applied to the customer job’s outstanding transactions, beginning with the oldest one. If `is_auto_apply` is false, QuickBooks receives the payment but doesn’t apply it to any outstanding transaction.

discount_account_ref.description: Refers to the account where this discount is tracked. In a request, if a `discount_account_ref` aggregate includes both `full_name` and `list_id`, `full_name` will be ignored.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

discount_class_ref.description: Class reference used in the Discount object.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

payment_amount.description: Represents the amount assigned to a particular receivable. The sum of all `payment_amount` elements in any given receive payment transaction must not be greater than `total_amount`.

applied_amount.description: Amount of a credit that is applied to a customer’s invoice, or amount of a payment that is applied to a particular bill or vendor credit.

credit_txn_id.description: The ID of the credit memo that you are applying to this invoice or bill.

txn_id.description: `txn_id` is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. `txn_id` values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

ar_account_ref.description: `ar_account_ref` points to an Accounts Receivable account. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

credit_card_txn_info.description: Contains data from the credit card transaction used in the payment. This data originates from a previous qbmsXML credit card transaction. The data following the element `credit_card_txn_input_info`” data is the data from the original qbmsXML request. The “`credit_card_txn_result_info`” is the data from the original qbmsXML response.

credit_card_txn_input_info.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. get.description:
qbXML: `PayrollDetailReportQueryRq`, from qbXML 3.0.

Returns information from any of five QuickBooks payroll reports:

- Employee state taxes detail report
- Payroll item detail report (lists the payroll transactions on which each payroll item appears)
- Payroll detail review report (provides detailed information about how QuickBooks calculates tax amounts on employee paychecks and in year-to-date transactions)
- Payroll transaction detail report (shows the line-item detail that appears on each payroll transaction)
- Payroll transactions by payee report (lists payroll transactions, grouping them by payee)

Payroll Summary Reports can be generated if your application is accessing a company file that is currently signed up for a subscription to a payroll service. (If your application isn’t signed up, it will receive an error when it attempts to generate a report in this category.)

The restrictions noted above about payroll reports requiring the use of the Intuit Payroll service don’t apply to the QuickBooks sample companies. You can still test out these reports on the sample companies without subscribing to the payroll service. For all other companies, however, the company must be subscribed.

Intuit's reference: [PayrollDetailReportQuery](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/payrolldetailreportquery).
