Choose at most one of: `list_id`, or `full_name`, or the set (`active_status`, `from_modified_date`, `max_returned`, `name_filter`, `name_range_filter`, `to_modified_date`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: active_status

parameters.description:
Filters results to objects modified on or after this timestamp. QuickBooks Desktop accepts 1970-01-01 through 2038-01-19T03:14:07. If only a date is provided, time defaults to 00:00:00.

Choose at most one of: `list_id`, or `full_name`, or the set (`active_status`, `from_modified_date`, `max_returned`, `name_filter`, `name_range_filter`, `to_modified_date`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: from_modified_date

parameters.description:
`full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

Choose at most one of: `list_id`, or `full_name`, or the set (`active_status`, `from_modified_date`, `max_returned`, `name_filter`, `name_range_filter`, `to_modified_date`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: full_name

parameters.description:
`list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

Choose at most one of: `list_id`, or `full_name`, or the set (`active_status`, `from_modified_date`, `max_returned`, `name_filter`, `name_range_filter`, `to_modified_date`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: list_id

parameters.description:
Limits the number of objects that a query returns. (To get a count of how many objects could possibly be returned, use the `meta_data` query attribute.) If you include a `max_returned` value, it must be at least 1.

Choose at most one of: `list_id`, or `full_name`, or the set (`active_status`, `from_modified_date`, `max_returned`, `name_filter`, `name_range_filter`, `to_modified_date`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: max_returned

parameters.description:

parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`. Send one with every request: it is how answers are delivered. Optional only so a script can queue and look up `links.self` by hand. It must be an absolute http or https URL. It may not contain a username or password, and in production it may not point at localhost or a private, loopback or link-local address.
parameters.name: webhook_url

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`. Send one with every request: it is how answers are delivered. Optional only so a script can queue and look up `links.self` by hand. It must be an absolute http or https URL. It may not contain a username or password, and in production it may not point at localhost or a private, loopback or link-local address.
parameters.name: webhook_url

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. get.description:
qbXML: `PayrollSummaryReportQueryRq`, from qbXML 3.0.

This report returns information from any of three QuickBooks payroll reports:

- **Payroll summary report:** This report shows the total wages, taxes withheld, deductions from net pay, additions to net pay, and employer-paid taxes and contributions for each employee on the payroll.
- **Employee earnings summary report:** This report shows information similar to the payroll summary report, but in a different layout. The report has a row for each employee and a column for each payroll item.
- **Payroll liability balances report:** This report lists the payroll liabilities the QuickBooks company owes to various agencies, such as the federal government, your state government, insurance plan administrators, labor unions, etc. The report covers unpaid liabilities incurred during the period of time shown in the From and To fields. If the company paid a liability incurred within the date range of the report, the report omits that liability, even if the payment occurred after the ending date of the report.

Payroll Summary Reports can be generated if your application is accessing a company file that is currently signed up for a subscription to a payroll service. (If your application isn’t signed up, it will receive an error when it attempts to generate a report in this category.)

The restrictions noted above about payroll reports requiring the use of the Intuit Payroll service don’t apply to the QuickBooks sample companies. You can still test out these reports on the sample companies without subscribing to the payroll service. For all other companies, however, the company must be subscribed.

Intuit's reference: [PayrollSummaryReportQuery](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/payrollsummaryreportquery).

qbXML: `PreferencesQueryRq`, from qbXML 1.1.

A PreferencesQueryRq request message returns information about many of the preferences that the QuickBooks user has set in the company file. Preferences can’t be modified through the SDK, only through the QuickBooks user interface. Note: If you include an explicit end tag in a PreferencesQueryRq request, you will receive an error if there is any space between the opening tag and the end tag. The following table shows valid and invalid ways of constructing this request:

- Valid (no space between opening and closing tags)

Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). * `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

Once you create a price level for a customer, QuickBooks will automatically use the custom price in new invoices, sales receipts, sales orders or credit memos for that customer. post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`. 201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

qbXML: `ReceivePaymentToDepositQueryRq`, from qbXML 2.0.

This query returns information about payments that have been received and are ready to deposit. You can use any returned `txn_id` and `txn_line_id` elements as PaymentTxnID and PaymentTxnLineID elements in subsequent DespositAdd requests. Note: If you include an explicit end tag in a ReceivePaymentToDepositQuery request, you will receive an error if there is any space between the opening tag and the end tag. The following table shows valid and invalid ways of constructing this request:

- Valid (no space between opening and closing tags)
- Valid (combined opening and closing tag)
- Invalid (space between opening and closing tags)

Intuit's reference: [ReceivePaymentToDepositQuery](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/receivepaymenttodepositquery).

get.description:
qbXML: `ReceivePaymentQueryRq`, from qbXML 1.1.

Finds received payments: exact ones by `txn_id` or `ref_number`, or a filtered set by customer (`entity_filter`), date or account. What each payment paid (its applied_to_txn_ret) comes back only with `include_line_items`, though a payment has no lines: without it, a payment applied to invoices answers none. Each applied_to_txn_ret's balance_remaining and txn_date are the invoice's as it is now, not when the payment was made (both observed on QuickBooks Enterprise 24.0, 2026-10-10). Set `iterator` to page through many results.

Intuit's reference: [ReceivePaymentQuery](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/receivepaymentquery).

parameters.description:
Filters according to the account name or `list_id`. If the “Use account numbers” preference is enabled in the QuickBooks company file, you can specify an account number (instead of an account name) for `full_name` and get the account you’re looking for. But if numbers have been used as account names, confusion could arise.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: account_filter

list_id.description: `list_id` and `full_name` both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

full_name.description: `full_name` (along with `list_id`) is a way to identify a list object. The `full_name` is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. `full_name` values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id_with_children.description: Allows you to filter for data that relates to the specified object and its descendants.

full_name_with_children.description: Allows you to filter for data that relates to the specified object and its descendants. For names that don’t have children, `full_name_with_children` is exactly the same as `full_name`.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. put.description:
qbXML: `ReceivePaymentModRq`, from qbXML 6.0. The `receive_payment_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Modifies a receive payment transaction. If you save QBMS credit card data in your ReceivePayments, this Mod request allows you to capture a previously authorized credit card charge. The way this works is that the ReceivePaymentAdd would contain the QBMS `credit_card_txn_info` aggregate with the `credit_card_txn_type` set to “Authorization,” which causes QB to internally mark the transaction as pending.

When the capture transaction is performed later, in QBMS, that capture transaction can be saved into QuickBooks via this Mod request, as you are modifying the original ReceivePayment but changing its `credit_card_txn_type` from”Authorization” to “Capture.” This mod operation results in the removal of the pending status and the posting of this receive payment.

Notice that the reconciliation data fields (`recon_batch_id`, `payment_grouping_code`, `payment_status`, `txn_authorization_time`, `txn_authorization_stamp`, `client_trans_id`) are optional ONLY if the `credit_card_txn_type` is “Authorization” because authorizations don’t have such data. If the type is “Charge”, then those reconciliation fields must be supplied or you will get a runtime error.

Intuit's reference, linked below, has the rest of these notes.

Intuit's reference: [ReceivePaymentMod](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/receivepaymentmod).

applied_amount.description: Amount of a credit that is applied to a customer’s invoice, or amount of a payment that is applied to a particular bill or vendor credit.

credit_txn_id.description: The ID of the credit memo that you are applying to this invoice or bill.

ar_account_ref.description: `ar_account_ref` points to an Accounts Receivable account. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored.

QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

credit_card_txn_info_mod.description: Contains data from the credit card transaction used in the payment. This data originates from a previous qbmsXML credit card transaction. The data following the element `credit_card_txn_input_info`” data is the data from the original qbmsXML request. The “`credit_card_txn_result_info`” is the data from the original qbmsXML response.

credit_card_txn_input_info_mod.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info_mod.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. This value is returned in the QBMS response to a QBMS transaction request, and must be subsequently supplied by your application in the QB SDK ReceivePaymentAdd or SalesReceiptAdd request.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. You should save this value without modification and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you want to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

txn_authorization_time.description: Timestamp indicating the time in which the card processor authorized the transaction.

customer_ref.description: `customer_ref` identifies a customer or customer job. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored. In SalesReceipt and ReceivePayment, it identifies who receives credit. In TimeTracking, it identifies who the time can be billed to and is required in TimeTrackingAdd when IsBillable is true.

QuickBooks assigns `list_id` when the object is created. `list_id` values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

deposit_to_account_ref.description: Refers to the account where these funds will be (or have been) deposited. In a ReceivePaymentAdd request, the default is Undeposited Funds if this isn’t included in the request. In a request, if a `deposit_to_account_ref` aggregate includes both `full_name` and `list_id`, `full_name` will be ignored.

exchange_rate.description: `exchange_rate` is the rate from this currency to the company’s home currency at AsOfDate. You can supply a rate when adding transactions, but QuickBooks does not provide rates through the SDK. If your home currency is USD and internet access is available, rates can be downloaded in the QuickBooks UI via Lists > Currency > Activities > Download Latest Exchange Rates.

memo.description: The beginning of this memo will appear in reports that show details of this receive payment.

payment_method_ref.description: `payment_method_ref` identifies how a payment is made (for example, cash, check, or card type). If both `full_name` and `list_id` are provided, `full_name` is ignored.

If both `full_name` and `list_id` are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses `list_id` and ignores `full_name`.

ref_number.description: `ref_number` is a user-managed transaction reference (for example, a check number). It can be edited and is not guaranteed to be globally unique. Some transaction types auto-populate `ref_number` when omitted, based on QuickBooks preferences and numbering state.

request_id.description: Your own label for the request, sent to QuickBooks as its qbXML `requestID` and echoed in the raw answer (`response_xml`); optional, since the answer's webhook already carries the request's `id`.

txn_date.description: The date of the transaction. In some cases, if you leave `txn_date` out of an -Add message, QuickBooks will prefill `txn_date` with the date of the last-saved transaction of the same type.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. A `3200` (`stale_edit_sequence`: the record changed after you read it) usually comes with the record as it stands in `response_json.error.current`, its current `edit_sequence` included: re-apply your change and send it again with that `edit_sequence` (without `current`, query the record first). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued-requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id` and each with its own `page_request_id` and `page`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last page, which can arrive before earlier ones, so the import is complete once every page from 1 to the `done` page's `page` has been handled. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` plus `state`. A `retryable` webhook is not final: the answer that follows carries the same `id` and `page_request_id` with a different `state`, and only a repeat of the same `state` is a duplicate.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

post.description:
qbXML: `SalesOrderAddRq`, from qbXML 2.1. The `sales_order_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Adds a sales order: goods a customer has ordered, often on back order, to be invoiced when they ship. A sales order doesn't post to any account. `customer_ref` is required, and lines go in `sales_order_line_add`. Sales orders need QuickBooks Premier or above. An invoice made from a sales order needs a sales tax item, so set `item_sales_tax_ref` if the company charges sales tax.

You can create Sales Orders only with QuickBooks Premier and above. However, if you are accessing a company file created in Premier and above from a lesser edition of QuickBooks (such as Pro), you should be able to do queries against SalesOrders and also Mods.

Since a sales order is a non-posting transaction, QuickBooks business logic doesn’t require the sales tax information at the point where the SalesOrder is added. (In the OSR this is an optional field.) However, the sales tax item IS required for the invoice. So if the SalesOrder doesn’t have a sales tax item set for it, you need to modify it so that it does have one before you create an invoice using that sales order.

Intuit's reference: [SalesOrderAdd](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/salesorderadd).
